citation_with_page: Rule: mortality is high where relief is late restricted or absent; applied to Orissa 1866; outcome per https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orissa_famine_of_1866 (constructed track record scored in hindsight of the famine itself; events row famine_mortality_high_without_early_relief/Orissa-Bengal-1866)
Same rule applied to Rajputana 1868-70; outcome per https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajputana_famine_of_1869 (constructed track record)
Same rule applied to Bihar 1873-74 (early relief so low mortality predicted); outcome per https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bihar_famine_of_1873%E2%80%931874 (constructed track record)
Same rule applied to Madras and Bombay 1876-78; outcome per https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Famine_of_1876%E2%80%931878 (constructed track record)

Same rule applied to 1899-1900: Famine Code relief was in place so low mortality predicted; outcome high (462000 deaths in Bombay Presidency; about one million in British districts) per https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_famine_of_1899%E2%80%931900 (a miss; constructed track record)
